h2: Liquid penetrant testing services in Portland: ship repair, shop welds and cold-weather practice
html:
Liquid penetrant testing services in Portland: ship repair, shop welds and cold-weather practice

Liquid penetrant testing in Portland is mostly field and shop work on non-magnetic material. That includes stainless and copper-nickel piping, propellers and shafting on vessels docked at Swan Island, and stainless or aluminum fabrication in shops around the port. Atlantis, based in Houston, sends PT technicians with visible-dye or fluorescent systems chosen to suit the part and the setting.

Ship repair. Vigor Marine Group is headquartered in Portland, and its original shipyard is on Swan Island. The largest of its three docks, the floating dock The Vigorous, is 960 feet long and arrived in 2014. Docked work brings a predictable PT workload. Propeller blade repairs and ground areas, stainless and copper-nickel seawater piping, shaft seal and stern gear components, and aluminum fittings are all common items. Class and owner repair procedures normally call for penetrant examination after a propeller or alloy weld repair, and often between repair stages. On a busy dock, that means the PT technician has to be there when the welder or grinder finishes, not a day later.

Shops and the Vancouver side. Fabrication shops building stainless spools, vessel parts and structural assemblies use PT for weld and machined-surface acceptance to ASME Section V Article 6 or AWS. Vigor's smaller Vancouver, Washington facility and the shops on that side of the Columbia fall under Washington rules. For example, pressure vessels there are under the Department of Labor & Industries. Each job names the jurisdiction and the acceptance code before work starts.

Portland weather and penetrant. Standard ASME penetrant procedures are qualified between 40 and 125 °F (5 and 52 °C). Portland winter mornings outdoors, on a dock or in an unheated bay, can fall below that range. The choices are to warm the part and keep it within the range through the dwell time, to use a procedure qualified for the lower temperature, or to move the work indoors. Rain and condensation also have to be dried off before the penetrant goes on, because water in a crack keeps the penetrant out. These decisions go into the procedure before the crew arrives.

  • Propeller and alloy weld repairs: PT after repair and between stages
  • Stainless and copper-nickel seawater piping on docked vessels
  • Shop welds and machined surfaces to ASME Section V Article 6 or AWS
  • Cold-weather limits and surface drying written into the procedure

If a part is going into an aerospace prime's supply chain under Nadcap-controlled fluorescent penetrant, it needs an accredited process line. Atlantis can support the written practice and procedures for that line through its outsourced Level III consulting.

Routing. Nationally, the method is covered on penetrant testing. For weld acceptance work, see Portland weld inspection; shipyard program support is on maritime NDT consulting in Portland. To train technicians, see penetrant testing training or the Practical NDT simulator for Portland. Send part materials, sizes and the governing code through the Portland PT enquiry.
